claim: On revision r806919.Wizard_1_610, CharacterNames.xml name tables use a required Name attribute, an optional Locale attribute, exactly one non-empty Section child, and ordered CharacterName text keys; for each resolved locale, the extractor returns each row as a LocaleKey and the matching localized Text from the section's .lang file.
disproof: A repeat against the same revision that finds a different accepted table attribute or child shape, locale-resolution rule, row order, or mapping into CharacterNameTable and CharacterNamePart refutes this claim.
evidence: ReadNameTables requires a CharacterNameTable root and accepts each direct table as <Table Name="..."> with a non-empty Name; Locale is optional, but must not be empty when present.
A table must contain exactly one non-empty Section and may contain CharacterName children; the trimmed text of each CharacterName is retained in source order as a locale key.

The Section text selects a .lang stem. With no Locale attribute, the extractor expands the table to each locale containing that stem; with Locale, it resolves that locale and removes a matching locale suffix from the stem.
For each resolved locale the extractor creates a CharacterNameTable with Name, Locale, and Parts; every part stores the source key in LocaleKey and the matching .lang value in Text.
how_to_repeat: Run the extractor's names dry run against your own r806919.Wizard_1_610 install and record the table and part counts it reports.
Inspect CharacterNames.xml and the matching Locale/<locale>/<section-stem>.lang files in your own install without copying their contents.
Compare the table attributes, direct child elements, locale expansion, and row mapping with CharacterNameExtractor::ReadNameTables and the CharacterNameTable and CharacterNamePart types.
